## Claim — `domain:ui` execution seat, R19

- **Session**: `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`
- **Branch**: `claude/issue-7196-stale-held-key-census`
- **Domain**: `ui` · **Worktree**: dedicated, off `origin/main` (`2d83cedc5` or later)
- **Clause ②**: ⛔ **not engaged.** Nothing declared moves — this corrects a comment and a local type's documentation of an intersection that already matches. No behaviour change, no export change.
- **Serial constraints cleared**: `ObjectGrid.tsx` was edited by three PRs today (#7167, #7186 and #7193, all landed or armed) and no lane currently holds it. ⚠️ The dispatch order tells this lane to re-derive on current `main` and expect line numbers to have moved.

Dispatched immediately because it is small, unambiguous, and free of the tier — a rare combination in this queue today (1 of 7 candidates read across R18/R19 were dispatchable as filed; see #6853).

⚠️ The scope note from the body is carried into the order as a ruling, because it is the part most likely to be skipped: **a hold list that is stale in one entry has no claim to be current in the others**, so the whole census gets re-derived, not read. But ⛔ this card does **not** assert the other entries are wrong — only that nobody has checked.

## ✅ LANDED — PR #7202 squash-merged to `main` (`f08cbd996`)

Verified **by content with a live control**:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| SUBJECT — the corrected census prose now cites **#6882** | **9** lines |
| CONTROL — `ObjectGridDataTableSchemaHolds` still present | **3** |

⭐ That control is the point, not a formality: the type was **kept deliberately**, with its docblock rewritten to explain why it survives as a redundancy. A probe that only checked "the stale sentence is gone" would pass equally if the whole type had been deleted — which was explicitly *not* the deliverable.

## ⭐ The ruling earned itself six times over

I ruled *"re-derive the WHOLE census, not just the named entry — a hold list stale in one entry has no claim to be current in the others."*

**16 claims re-derived. SEVEN defective. The card named ONE.**

And they split two ways, which I did not anticipate:

- **4 stale** — true when written, drifted since. Including **`cellClassName` carrying the SAME "pending ruling" prose, settled by the SAME #6882 ruling** — a second instance of the card's own defect, sitting beside it, unmentioned.
- **3 wrong when written** — false on the day, dated to `beccf1c6b`. One claimed *"the 7-literal union"* when it had been **eight since #6370 landed a day earlier**, in a PR whose own subject line says "8-literal".

⚠️ The second kind is the more alarming, and it was nowhere in the card. "Stale" implies a document once accurate — ordinary decay. These had **no moment at which a reader could have trusted them**, and no drift to detect.

## ⭐ And the root cause was diagnosed, not just the symptoms

> the censuses are guarded **asymmetrically** — the column-level hold's **entry condition** is pinned (`columnHoldsExpiry-6424.test.ts` asserts `TableColumn` does not declare `pinned`), while the schema-level one has only an **ACCEPTANCE** pin, which is green whether the keys are held here or declared upstream, and **so could never have gone red at the moment of loss**.

⇒ That is *why this census rotted and its twin did not*. The general lesson outlives the card: **a pin that stays green on both sides of the event it exists to catch is not a guard.** It looks like coverage, runs on every CI, and is structurally incapable of failing. Filed as **#7201**.

## The nine clean claims are a real result

Every column-level verdict (`headerIcon`, `pinned`, `wrap`, `options`, `essential`, `name`) and the `FieldType` count of 49 re-derived correctly. ⭐ *"The others are correct"* is now **measured rather than assumed** — the epistemic state a future reader actually needs, and precisely what a fix confined to the named entry would have left undone.

A2.2 was confirmed properly: each hold's shape is **`Equal`** (not merely `extends`) to the upstream member, and the two are **mutually assignable in both directions**. Checking both ways is what makes "identical" a measurement rather than a one-directional subtype check that would pass on a narrower hold.

⚠️ **No ablation, and none owed** — *"the diff adds and removes no assertion; the one assertion touched keeps its exact shape and only its name and docblock change."* Stating why an ablation would measure nothing beats running a ceremonial one.

## Downstream

**#6919** was found during dedupe, correctly not touched, and is now ruled: it **stays open**, re-scoped to the hold's actual **removal**, and `pm:blocked` on the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` quota (deleting a member from an exported type narrows published surface). This PR discharged its *first* half — the prohibition is lifted and the redundancy is recorded with measurements. ⛔ Closing it would have lost the only tracker for a removal deliberately not made. That card was also carrying **no labels at all**, which is why it had been invisible to every sweep.

Clearing `pm:dispatched`.
